reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it focuses on building a solid aerobic base with targeted threshold work and hill sessions, while Plan B prioritizes longer, less structured runs. Plan B's emphasis on longer, easier runs, while beneficial for endurance, doesn't provide the same level of targeted stimulus needed for significant speed improvements. Furthermore, Plan A’s more conservative approach to volume and recovery, with two rest days, is likely more appropriate for someone seeking to improve speed without risking overtraining.
